name: Thales of Miletus
shortBio: Considered the first Western philosopher, proposing naturalistic explanations for the cosmos rather than mythical ones.
centralQuestion: What is the primary substance (arche) underlying all change?

keyWorks.title: On the Solstice and Equinox
keyWorks.description: Major work by Thales of Miletus.

name: Heraclitus of Ephesus
shortBio: Known as 'The Obscure', famous for his doctrine that universal flux is governed by an underlying cosmic Logos.
centralQuestion: How does unity emerge from perpetual change and strife?

keyWorks.title: Fragments (On Nature)
keyWorks.description: Major work by Heraclitus of Ephesus.

name: Parmenides of Elea
shortBio: Founder of Eleatic metaphysics; argued through pure deductive logic that Being is singular, eternal, and change is an illusion.
centralQuestion: What does reason prove about the nature of What-Is versus What-Is-Not?

keyWorks.title: On Nature (Poem)
keyWorks.description: Major work by Parmenides of Elea.

name: Democritus
shortBio: The 'Laughing Philosopher' who pioneered the mechanical atomic theory of matter moving through void space.
centralQuestion: Can macroscopic reality be reduced to indivisible physical units?

keyWorks.title: The Great Diakosmos
keyWorks.description: Major work by Democritus.

name: Socrates
shortBio: Athenian street philosopher who redirected philosophy from cosmology to human ethics and self-examination via the elenchus dialectic.
centralQuestion: What is virtue, and how should one live an examined life?

keyWorks.title: Oral teaching recorded by Plato and Xenophon
keyWorks.description: Major work by Socrates.

name: Plato
shortBio: Founder of the Academy in Athens. Developed the Theory of Forms, the Allegory of the Cave, and ideal political constitutions.
centralQuestion: What is the true nature of reality, justice, and the immortal soul?

keyWorks.title: The Republic
keyWorks.description: Socratic dialogue on justice, the ideal city-state, the Allegory of the Cave, and the philosopher-king.

keyWorks.title: Symposium
keyWorks.description: Dialogue exploring the nature and origin of Eros (love) and the ascent to the Form of Beauty.

keyWorks.title: Phaedo
keyWorks.description: Recounts Socrates' final hours in prison, arguing for the immortality of the soul and the Theory of Forms.

keyWorks.title: Timaeus
keyWorks.description: Plato's speculative cosmology describing the Demiurge fashioning the cosmos according to eternal Forms.

keyWorks.title: Meno
keyWorks.description: Investigates whether virtue can be taught, introducing the theory of recollection (anamnesis).

name: Aristotle
shortBio: Plato's greatest student and tutor to Alexander the Great. Systematized logic, biology, physics, metaphysics, and teleological virtue ethics.
centralQuestion: What is the telos (purpose) of things, and what constitutes human flourishing (eudaimonia)?

keyWorks.title: Nicomachean Ethics
keyWorks.description: Foundational treatise on virtue ethics, the Golden Mean, and human flourishing (eudaimonia).

keyWorks.title: Metaphysics
keyWorks.description: Inquiry into 'Being qua Being', substance, potentiality and actuality, and the Unmoved Mover.

keyWorks.title: Politics
keyWorks.description: Examination of political constitutions, citizenship, and man as inherently a 'political animal'.

keyWorks.title: De Anima
keyWorks.description: Aristotle's psychology: the soul as the formal actuality of an organic physical body.

keyWorks.title: Organon
keyWorks.description: The six treatises establishing categorical logic and the deductive syllogism.

name: Epicurus
shortBio: Founded The Garden. Taught that the greatest good is tranquility (ataraxia) and freedom from fear of death and gods.
centralQuestion: How do we attain peace of mind through modest desires and true friendship?

keyWorks.title: Letter to Menoeceus
keyWorks.description: Major work by Epicurus.

keyWorks.title: Principal Doctrines
keyWorks.description: Major work by Epicurus.

name: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
shortBio: Roman Stoic statesman, playwright, and advisor to Nero. Wrote profoundly practical treatises on anger, brevity of life, and resilience.
centralQuestion: How do we live with dignity and serenity amid political chaos and mortality?

keyWorks.title: Letters from a Stoic (Epistulae Morales)
keyWorks.description: 124 letters advising Lucilius on practical Stoic wisdom, overcoming fear of death, and resilience.

keyWorks.title: On the Shortness of Life
keyWorks.description: Essay asserting life is long if spent wisely, but short if squandered on frivolous ambition.

keyWorks.title: On Anger
keyWorks.description: Stoic psychological analysis of anger as temporary madness and how reason can extinguish it.

name: Epictetus
shortBio: Born a slave in Hierapolis, Epictetus taught that mental freedom comes from distinguishing what is within our control from what is not.
centralQuestion: What is in our power, and how do we master our own judgments?

keyWorks.title: Discourses
keyWorks.description: Informal lectures recorded by Arrian on Stoic ethics and the Dichotomy of Control.

keyWorks.title: Enchiridion (Handbook)
keyWorks.description: Concise practical handbook of Stoic advice for mental tranquility and moral freedom.

name: Marcus Aurelius
shortBio: Roman Emperor and last of the Five Good Emperors. Recorded private journal meditations on duty, death, and cosmological solidarity.
centralQuestion: How does one rule an empire while keeping the soul uncorrupted and aligned with nature?

keyWorks.title: Meditations
keyWorks.description: Private spiritual journal of Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius on duty, nature, and virtue.

name: Pyrrho of Elis
shortBio: Pioneer of Skepticism; traveled to India with Alexander. Held that things are indifferently indeterminable, advocating epoche.
centralQuestion: Can peace of mind be attained by withholding all dogmatic belief?

keyWorks.title: Oral tradition recorded by Timon and Sextus Empiricus
keyWorks.description: Major work by Pyrrho of Elis.

name: Plotinus
shortBio: Architect of Neoplatonism; described reality as a luminous cascade emanating from the transcendent 'One' down to the soul.
centralQuestion: How can the embodied soul re-ascend into mystical communion with the Source?

keyWorks.title: Enneads
keyWorks.description: Major work by Plotinus.

name: Laozi (Lao Tzu)
shortBio: Legendary author of the Daodejing, articulating the effortless harmony of Wu Wei and the unnameable Dao.
centralQuestion: How do we flow with the spontaneous principle of the natural cosmos?

keyWorks.title: Daodejing (Tao Te Ching)
keyWorks.description: Major work by Laozi (Lao Tzu).

name: Siddhartha Gautama (The Buddha)
shortBio: Indian spiritual teacher whose Four Noble Truths and doctrine of Anatta (no-self) revolutionized eastern phenomenology.
centralQuestion: What is the root of suffering (dukkha), and how is liberation achieved?

keyWorks.title: Pali Canon Discourses
keyWorks.description: Major work by Siddhartha Gautama (The Buddha).

name: Nagarjuna
shortBio: Founder of Madhyamaka Buddhism; demonstrated through rigorous dialectic that all phenomena are empty (sunyata) of intrinsic essence.
centralQuestion: How does dependent origination dissolve metaphysical absolutes?

keyWorks.title: Mulamadhyamakakarika (Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way)
keyWorks.description: Major work by Nagarjuna.

name: Adi Shankara
shortBio: Consolidator of Advaita Vedanta philosophy, proving that Atman (individual self) and Brahman (ultimate reality) are non-dual.
centralQuestion: How does knowledge of non-duality shatter the illusion (maya) of separation?

keyWorks.title: Brahma Sutra Bhasya
keyWorks.description: Major work by Adi Shankara.

keyWorks.title: Upadesasahasri
keyWorks.description: Major work by Adi Shankara.

name: Augustine of Hippo
shortBio: Bishop of Hippo who synthesized Christian theology with Neoplatonism; explored memory, psychological time, original sin, and grace.
centralQuestion: What is the relation between divine eternity and the human consciousness in time?

keyWorks.title: Confessions
keyWorks.description: Autobiographical spiritual journey, theology of grace, and famous analysis of the psychological nature of time.

keyWorks.title: City of God
keyWorks.description: Philosophy of history contrasting the heavenly City of God with the earthly City of Man after the sack of Rome.

keyWorks.title: On the Trinity
keyWorks.description: Major work by Augustine of Hippo.

name: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
shortBio: Polymath of the Islamic Golden Age; authored the Floating Man thought experiment and distinction between essence and existence.
centralQuestion: Can self-consciousness exist independent of bodily senses?

keyWorks.title: The Book of Healing
keyWorks.description: Major work by Ibn Sina (Avicenna).

keyWorks.title: The Canon of Medicine
keyWorks.description: Major work by Ibn Sina (Avicenna).

name: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
shortBio: The 'Great Commentator' on Aristotle whose defense of rational philosophy against Al-Ghazali shaped the European Renaissance.
centralQuestion: Can religious faith and demonstrative philosophical reasoning harmoniously coexist?

keyWorks.title: The Incoherence of the Incoherence
keyWorks.description: Major work by Ibn Rushd (Averroes).

keyWorks.title: The Decisive Treatise
keyWorks.description: Major work by Ibn Rushd (Averroes).

name: Thomas Aquinas
shortBio: Dominican friar and prince of Scholasticism. Harmonized Christian revelation with Aristotle; formulated the Five Ways to prove God's existence.
centralQuestion: How do faith and reason cooperate in the pursuit of ultimate truth?

keyWorks.title: Summa Theologiae
keyWorks.description: Aquinas's masterwork of medieval scholasticism, containing the Five Ways to demonstrate God's existence.

keyWorks.title: Summa contra Gentiles
keyWorks.description: Major work by Thomas Aquinas.

name: William of Ockham
shortBio: Franciscan philosopher famous for Ockham's Razor and Nominalism (universals are mere names, not real metaphysical entities).
centralQuestion: Should entities ever be multiplied beyond necessity?

keyWorks.title: Summa Logicae
keyWorks.description: Major work by William of Ockham.

name: Niccolò Machiavelli
shortBio: Florentine diplomat who established political realism, analyzing how power is practically seized and maintained.
centralQuestion: Is it better for a leader to be loved or feared, and how must virtue adapt to fortuna?

keyWorks.title: The Prince
keyWorks.description: Realistic political treatise on statecraft, the balance of virtù and fortuna, and maintaining power.

keyWorks.title: Discourses on Livy
keyWorks.description: Major work by Niccolò Machiavelli.

name: Francis Bacon
shortBio: Father of the scientific method and champion of empiricism; exposed the Idols of the Mind that distort human inquiry.
centralQuestion: How can systematic empirical induction give humanity mastery over nature?

keyWorks.title: Novum Organum
keyWorks.description: Major work by Francis Bacon.

keyWorks.title: The New Atlantis
keyWorks.description: Major work by Francis Bacon.

name: Thomas Hobbes
shortBio: Social contract theorist who described life in the state of nature as 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'.
centralQuestion: How do self-interested individuals construct a sovereign commonwealth to escape civil war?

keyWorks.title: Leviathan
keyWorks.description: Foundational political philosophy on the state of nature, the social contract, and the sovereign Leviathan.

name: René Descartes
shortBio: Father of modern Western philosophy. Used radical methodical doubt to discover the bedrock certainty: 'Cogito, ergo sum'.
centralQuestion: What can be known with absolute epistemological certainty?

keyWorks.title: Meditations on First Philosophy
keyWorks.description: Descartes' radical doubt, the Cogito, proof of God, and mind-body substance dualism.

keyWorks.title: Discourse on the Method
keyWorks.description: Autobiographical treatise introducing Cartesian skepticism and the scientific method.

name: Baruch Spinoza
shortBio: Excommunicated Jewish-Dutch philosopher who developed geometric pantheism: God and Nature are one single infinite substance (Deus Sive Natura).
centralQuestion: How does understanding necessity and cosmic unity liberate the human mind from passive passions?

keyWorks.title: Ethics (demonstrated in geometrical order)
keyWorks.description: Geometrical proof of pantheistic monism: God and Nature as one infinite substance (Deus Sive Natura).

keyWorks.title: Tractatus Theologico-Politicus
keyWorks.description: Major work by Baruch Spinoza.

name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
shortBio: Polymath co-inventor of calculus. Conceived reality as an infinite harmony of windowless spiritual atoms called monads.
centralQuestion: Why is there something rather than nothing, and is this the best of all possible worlds?

keyWorks.title: Monadology
keyWorks.description: Leibniz's late metaphysical synthesis: reality composed of immaterial, perception-bearing monads in pre-established harmony.

keyWorks.title: Discourse on Metaphysics
keyWorks.description: Major work by Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz.

keyWorks.title: Theodicy
keyWorks.description: Major work by Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz.

name: John Locke
shortBio: Pioneer of British Empiricism and constitutional democracy. Argued the mind begins as a blank slate (tabula rasa).
centralQuestion: How do ideas enter the mind through sensation and reflection, and what justifies government?

keyWorks.title: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding
keyWorks.description: Argues against innate ideas; formulates the mind as a blank slate (tabula rasa) populated through sensation.

keyWorks.title: Two Treatises of Government
keyWorks.description: Foundational theory of natural rights (life, liberty, property) and government by consent of the governed.

name: George Berkeley
shortBio: Irish philosopher who advanced subjective idealism: material objects exist solely in being perceived ('Esse est percipi').
centralQuestion: Does matter exist independently of minds and perceptual experience?

keyWorks.title: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge
keyWorks.description: Major work by George Berkeley.

keyWorks.title: Three Dialogues between Hylas and Philonous
keyWorks.description: Major work by George Berkeley.

name: David Hume
shortBio: Scottish skeptic who dismantled dogmatic rationalism, questioning causality, the unified self (bundle theory), and induction.
centralQuestion: Can reason justify our belief in cause and effect or an enduring personal self?

keyWorks.title: A Treatise of Human Nature
keyWorks.description: Hume's empirical masterpiece investigating human knowledge, passions, morality, and the bundle theory of self.

keyWorks.title: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding
keyWorks.description: Refined presentation of Hume's epistemological skepticism, problem of induction, and critique of miracles.

name: Adam Smith
shortBio: Key thinker of the Scottish Enlightenment; explored human moral psychology through sympathy and economic organization.
centralQuestion: How does mutual moral sympathy and division of labor produce social flourishing?

keyWorks.title: The Theory of Moral Sentiments
keyWorks.description: Major work by Adam Smith.

keyWorks.title: The Wealth of Nations
keyWorks.description: Major work by Adam Smith.

name: Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet)
shortBio: Enlightenment wit and champion of civil liberties, religious tolerance, freedom of speech, and satire against dogmatic optimism.
centralQuestion: How do we crush fanaticism and cultivate our own garden with reason?

keyWorks.title: Candide
keyWorks.description: Satirical philosophical novella mocking Leibnizian theological optimism ('best of all possible worlds').

keyWorks.title: Philosophical Letters
keyWorks.description: Major work by Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet).

keyWorks.title: Treatise on Tolerance
keyWorks.description: Major work by Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet).

name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
shortBio: Romantic political philosopher who argued man is born free but everywhere in chains, corrupted by unequal property and pride.
centralQuestion: How can human freedom and political sovereignty unite under the General Will?

keyWorks.title: The Social Contract
keyWorks.description: 'Man is born free, and he is everywhere in chains.' Articulates legitimate sovereignty and the General Will.

keyWorks.title: Discourse on Inequality
keyWorks.description: Major work by Jean-Jacques Rousseau.

keyWorks.title: Emile
keyWorks.description: Major work by Jean-Jacques Rousseau.

name: Immanuel Kant
shortBio: Revolutionized philosophy through Transcendental Idealism: our mind structures phenomenal experience, while the noumenon remains beyond.
centralQuestion: What can I know? What should I do? What may I hope?

keyWorks.title: Critique of Pure Reason
keyWorks.description: Copernican revolution in metaphysics: Transcendental Idealism, synthetic a priori judgments, and bounds of reason.

keyWorks.title: Critique of Practical Reason
keyWorks.description: Kant's second critique, proving freedom, immortality of the soul, and God through moral necessity.

keyWorks.title: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
keyWorks.description: Deontological ethics introducing the Categorical Imperative and the intrinsic dignity of persons.

name: G.W.F. Hegel
shortBio: Architect of dialectical idealism; saw history as the progressive self-realization and freedom of Absolute Spirit (Geist).
centralQuestion: How does reason unfold dialectically through history, culture, and recognition?

keyWorks.title: Phenomenology of Spirit
keyWorks.description: Dialectical journey of consciousness toward Absolute Knowing, including the Master-Slave dialectic.

keyWorks.title: Science of Logic
keyWorks.description: Major work by G.W.F. Hegel.

keyWorks.title: Elements of the Philosophy of Right
keyWorks.description: Major work by G.W.F. Hegel.

name: Arthur Schopenhauer
shortBio: Post-Kantian thinker who identified Kant's thing-in-itself as blind, insatiable Will; synthesized Western idealism with Buddhist and Upanishadic insights.
centralQuestion: How can the individual escape the suffering and striving of the metaphysical Will?

keyWorks.title: The World as Will and Representation
keyWorks.description: Post-Kantian masterpiece unveiling the thing-in-itself as blind, insatiable metaphysical Will.

keyWorks.title: On the Freedom of the Will
keyWorks.description: Major work by Arthur Schopenhauer.

name: Søren Kierkegaard
shortBio: Father of Christian existentialism; rejected Hegel's objective systems in favor of subjective truth, dread, and the leap of faith.
centralQuestion: What does it mean for an individual to exist before God with authentic passion?

keyWorks.title: Fear and Trembling
keyWorks.description: Kierkegaard's pseudonym Johannes de Silentio examines Abraham's sacrifice of Isaac and the leap of faith.

keyWorks.title: The Sickness Unto Death
keyWorks.description: Major work by Søren Kierkegaard.

keyWorks.title: Either/Or
keyWorks.description: Major work by Søren Kierkegaard.

name: Karl Marx
shortBio: Turned Hegel's dialectic on its head into historical materialism; analyzed class struggle, alienation, and capitalism's contradictions.
centralQuestion: How do material economic conditions shape consciousness, and how can the working class emancipate humanity?

keyWorks.title: Das Kapital
keyWorks.description: Critique of political economy, commodity fetishism, surplus value, and the mechanics of capitalist exploitation.

keyWorks.title: The Communist Manifesto
keyWorks.description: Major work by Karl Marx.

keyWorks.title: Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
keyWorks.description: Major work by Karl Marx.

name: Friedrich Nietzsche
shortBio: Radical iconoclast who proclaimed the 'death of God', analyzed the will to power, master/slave morality, and the challenge of the Übermensch.
centralQuestion: How can humanity overcome nihilism and affirm life without transcendent illusions?

keyWorks.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
keyWorks.description: Philosophical poem proclaiming the Death of God, the Übermensch (Overman), and the Eternal Recurrence.

keyWorks.title: Beyond Good and Evil
keyWorks.description: Polemic against traditional dogmatic morality, introducing perspectivism and the Will to Power.

keyWorks.title: On the Genealogy of Morality
keyWorks.description: Major work by Friedrich Nietzsche.

keyWorks.title: The Gay Science
keyWorks.description: Major work by Friedrich Nietzsche.

name: John Stuart Mill
shortBio: Liberal philosopher who refined utilitarian ethics (higher vs lower pleasures) and defended individual liberty and women's rights.
centralQuestion: What is the boundary between the authority of society and the liberty of the individual?

keyWorks.title: On Liberty
keyWorks.description: Classic liberal defense of individual autonomy, free speech, and the Harm Principle.

keyWorks.title: Utilitarianism
keyWorks.description: Major work by John Stuart Mill.

keyWorks.title: The Subjection of Women
keyWorks.description: Major work by John Stuart Mill.

name: William James
shortBio: Pioneer of American pragmatism and psychology; formulated the stream of consciousness and the 'cash value' theory of truth.
centralQuestion: What difference does an idea make in concrete human experience?

keyWorks.title: Pragmatism
keyWorks.description: Major work by William James.

keyWorks.title: The Varieties of Religious Experience
keyWorks.description: Major work by William James.

keyWorks.title: The Will to Believe
keyWorks.description: Major work by William James.

name: Edmund Husserl
shortBio: Founder of phenomenology. Advocated setting aside scientific presuppositions (epoché) to examine the intentional structures of consciousness.
centralQuestion: How does consciousness constitute meaning in lived experience?

keyWorks.title: Logical Investigations
keyWorks.description: Major work by Edmund Husserl.

keyWorks.title: Ideas Pertaining to a Pure Phenomenology
keyWorks.description: Major work by Edmund Husserl.

name: Martin Heidegger
shortBio: Ontologist who revived the question of Being; analyzed human existence as Dasein ('Being-in-the-world') oriented toward death.
centralQuestion: What is the meaning of Being, and how has Western metaphysics forgotten it?

keyWorks.title: Being and Time
keyWorks.description: Heidegger's fundamental ontology: analyzing human existence as Dasein ('Being-in-the-world') oriented toward death.

keyWorks.title: The Question Concerning Technology
keyWorks.description: Major work by Martin Heidegger.

name: Jean-Paul Sartre
shortBio: Existentialist titan who declared that 'existence precedes essence'; humans are condemned to be free and prone to bad faith.
centralQuestion: How does the individual take absolute responsibility for creating selfhood without excuses?

keyWorks.title: Being and Nothingness
keyWorks.description: Sartre's existentialist magnum opus on radical freedom, consciousness as nothingness, and bad faith.

keyWorks.title: Existentialism is a Humanism
keyWorks.description: Major work by Jean-Paul Sartre.

keyWorks.title: Nausea
keyWorks.description: Major work by Jean-Paul Sartre.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
shortBio: Existentialist and pioneering feminist philosopher; formulated that 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman'.
centralQuestion: How do social situations construct otherness and constrain human freedom?

keyWorks.title: The Second Sex
keyWorks.description: Foundational feminist philosophy: 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.' Analysis of feminine otherness.

keyWorks.title: The Ethics of Ambiguity
keyWorks.description: Major work by Simone de Beauvoir.

name: Albert Camus
shortBio: Philosopher of the Absurd: the clash between humanity's thirst for meaning and the silent indifference of the universe.
centralQuestion: Is life worth living despite the absurdity of existence?

keyWorks.title: The Myth of Sisyphus
keyWorks.description: Camus's philosophical essay on the absurd: 'One must imagine Sisyphus happy.'

keyWorks.title: The Stranger
keyWorks.description: Major work by Albert Camus.

keyWorks.title: The Rebel
keyWorks.description: Major work by Albert Camus.

name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
shortBio: Revolutionized philosophy twice: first with the logical picture theory of language, then with ordinary language games and forms of life.
centralQuestion: What can be said clearly, and what must be passed over in silence?

keyWorks.title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
keyWorks.description: Logical picture theory of language: 'Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.'

keyWorks.title: Philosophical Investigations
keyWorks.description: Later Wittgenstein: rejecting formal picture theory for ordinary language games and forms of life.

name: Bertrand Russell
shortBio: Leader of the British revolt against idealism, co-founder of analytic philosophy, logician, peace activist, and author of Principia Mathematica.
centralQuestion: Can mathematics be grounded entirely on formal logic?

keyWorks.title: Principia Mathematica
keyWorks.description: Major work by Bertrand Russell.

keyWorks.title: The Problems of Philosophy
keyWorks.description: Major work by Bertrand Russell.

keyWorks.title: On Denoting
keyWorks.description: Major work by Bertrand Russell.

name: Karl Popper
shortBio: Philosopher of science who replaced verification with falsificationism; defender of the open society against totalitarianism.
centralQuestion: What demarcates genuine science from pseudo-science?

keyWorks.title: The Logic of Scientific Discovery
keyWorks.description: Major work by Karl Popper.

keyWorks.title: The Open Society and Its Enemies
keyWorks.description: Major work by Karl Popper.

name: Theodor W. Adorno
shortBio: Leading figure of the Frankfurt School; critiqued the culture industry, instrumental reason, and authoritarianism.
centralQuestion: How did Enlightenment rationality turn into its opposite: barbarism and mass conformity?

keyWorks.title: Dialectic of Enlightenment
keyWorks.description: Major work by Theodor W. Adorno.

keyWorks.title: Minima Moralia
keyWorks.description: Major work by Theodor W. Adorno.

keyWorks.title: Negative Dialectics
keyWorks.description: Major work by Theodor W. Adorno.

name: Michel Foucault
shortBio: French historian of systems of thought; explored how power is entwined with knowledge, surveillance (Panopticon), and biopolitics.
centralQuestion: How do disciplinary institutions and discourses construct our conceptions of sanity, sexuality, and deviance?

keyWorks.title: Discipline and Punish
keyWorks.description: Foucault's genealogy of modern penal institutions, panopticism, and the birth of disciplinary power.

keyWorks.title: The History of Sexuality
keyWorks.description: Major work by Michel Foucault.

keyWorks.title: The Order of Things
keyWorks.description: Major work by Michel Foucault.

name: Jacques Derrida
shortBio: Creator of deconstruction; unmasked the hidden hierarchies and instabilities in Western metaphysics of presence.
centralQuestion: How does language continuously defer fixed meaning through différance?

keyWorks.title: Of Grammatology
keyWorks.description: Major work by Jacques Derrida.

keyWorks.title: Writing and Difference
keyWorks.description: Major work by Jacques Derrida.

name: Gilles Deleuze
shortBio: Metaphysician of immanence and multiplicity; replaced arborescent (tree-like) hierarchical thinking with rhizomatic networks.
centralQuestion: How can thought create new concepts based on difference rather than representation?

keyWorks.title: Difference and Repetition
keyWorks.description: Major work by Gilles Deleuze.

keyWorks.title: Anti-Oedipus
keyWorks.description: Major work by Gilles Deleuze.

keyWorks.title: A Thousand Plateaus
keyWorks.description: Major work by Gilles Deleuze.

name: Hannah Arendt
shortBio: Political theorist who analyzed totalitarianism, civic action in the public realm, and the terrifying 'banality of evil'.
centralQuestion: What preserves the space of public freedom and prevents thoughtless totalitarian evil?

keyWorks.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
keyWorks.description: Major work by Hannah Arendt.

keyWorks.title: The Human Condition
keyWorks.description: Major work by Hannah Arendt.

keyWorks.title: Eichmann in Jerusalem
keyWorks.description: Major work by Hannah Arendt.

name: John Rawls
shortBio: Revitalized political philosophy with 'justice as fairness', proposing principles chosen behind an impartial 'veil of ignorance'.
centralQuestion: What principles of social justice would rational equals choose in an unbiased original position?

keyWorks.title: A Theory of Justice
keyWorks.description: Revitalized political philosophy with 'justice as fairness' chosen behind the veil of ignorance.

keyWorks.title: Political Liberalism
keyWorks.description: Major work by John Rawls.

name: Byung-Chul Han
shortBio: German-Korean contemporary philosopher diagnosing digital burnout, self-exploitation, hyper-transparency, and the erosion of ritual.
centralQuestion: How does the neoliberal achievement society turn freedom into self-enslavement and fatigue?

keyWorks.title: The Burnout Society
keyWorks.description: Contemporary critique of the neoliberal achievement society where freedom transforms into compulsive self-exploitation.

keyWorks.title: The Agony of Eros
keyWorks.description: Major work by Byung-Chul Han.

keyWorks.title: The Disappearance of Rituals
keyWorks.description: Major work by Byung-Chul Han.

name: Nick Bostrom
shortBio: Contemporary philosopher known for foundational work on existential risk, the simulation argument, and artificial intelligence safety.
centralQuestion: Are we living in a computer simulation, and how can humanity navigate catastrophic technological risk?

keyWorks.title: Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
keyWorks.description: Foundational treatise on existential risk, artificial general intelligence trajectory, and value alignment.

keyWorks.title: The Simulation Argument
keyWorks.description: Major work by Nick Bostrom.

name: Zeno of Elea
shortBio: Disciple of Parmenides who invented dialectical reductio ad absurdum and formulated celebrated paradoxes of motion and infinite divisibility.
centralQuestion: How can motion and multiplicity be real if their mathematical premises yield insurmountable contradictions?

keyWorks.title: Paradoxes of Motion (Fragments)
keyWorks.description: Formulation of Achilles and the Tortoise, the Dichotomy, the Arrow, and the Moving Rows.

name: Confucius (Kongzi)
shortBio: Foundational teacher and philosopher of China whose ethical and political philosophy centered on humaneness (Ren), ritual propriety (Li), and moral self-cultivation.
centralQuestion: How can individuals cultivate moral excellence and restore harmonious societal governance through ritual and virtue?

keyWorks.title: The Analects (Lunyu)
keyWorks.description: Collection of sayings, dialogues, and historical anecdotes compiling Confucius's moral philosophy.

name: Zhuangzi (Chuang Tzu)
shortBio: Master Daoist sage whose parables, linguistic skepticism, and butterfly dream developed radical perspectivism, spiritual freedom, and effortless unity with the Dao.
centralQuestion: How can human consciousness transcend rigid dualisms of right and wrong to wander freely in spontaneous harmony with nature?

keyWorks.title: Zhuangzi (The Inner Chapters)
keyWorks.description: Foundational Daoist text celebrated for its philosophical depth, literary wit, and the Butterfly Dream.

name: Anselm of Canterbury
shortBio: Father of Scholasticism and Archbishop of Canterbury who formulated the canonical Ontological Argument for the existence of God in the Proslogion.
centralQuestion: Can the reality of God be demonstrated through pure conceptual analysis as 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'?

keyWorks.title: Proslogion
keyWorks.description: Famous treatise containing the ontological proof of God from the concept of maximal greatness.

keyWorks.title: Monologion
keyWorks.description: Theological meditation on divine attributes and faith seeking understanding.

name: Al-Ghazali (Algazel)
shortBio: Influential Persian Islamic theologian and jurist who critiqued Avicennian Aristotelianism and formulated occasionalism, anticipating Humean causal skepticism.
centralQuestion: Does human philosophical reason possess the capacity to prove necessary causal laws and transcendent metaphysical truths?

keyWorks.title: The Incoherence of the Philosophers (Tahafut al-Falasifa)
keyWorks.description: Landmark philosophical critique of Islamic Peripatetic philosophy and necessary causal connection.

keyWorks.title: Deliverance from Error (Al-Munqidh min al-Dalal)
keyWorks.description: Autobiographical spiritual treatise recounting his epistemological crisis and Sufi resolution.

name: Moses Maimonides (Rambam)
shortBio: Preeminent Sephardic Jewish philosopher and codifier whose Guide for the Perplexed reconciled Aristotelian metaphysics with biblical revelation through negative theology.
centralQuestion: How can rational philosophy and allegorical biblical revelation be harmonized without compromising divine incorporeality and negative theology?

keyWorks.title: The Guide for the Perplexed (Moreh Nevukhim)
keyWorks.description: Masterwork addressing philosophical perplexities arising from anthropomorphic biblical texts.

name: Michel de Montaigne
shortBio: French Renaissance humanist who pioneered the essay form and revived ancient Pyrrhonian skepticism with his motto 'Que sais-je?' (What do I know?), sparking modern epistemology.
centralQuestion: What can a fallible human truly know, and how should one conduct a virtuous life free from dogmatic intolerance?

keyWorks.title: Essais
keyWorks.description: Pioneering collection of introspective personal reflections, moral explorations, and skeptical inquiries.

keyWorks.title: Apology for Raymond Sebond
keyWorks.description: Extended essay deploying radical Pyrrhonian skepticism against human intellectual hubris.

name: Blaise Pascal
shortBio: French mathematician, physicist, and religious philosopher who formulated Pascal's Wager, explored the tragedy of human fallenness, and declared that 'the heart has its reasons which reason knows nothing of'.
centralQuestion: How does human consciousness navigate the abyss between nothingness and infinity, and why is faith an inescapable existential wager?

keyWorks.title: Pensées
keyWorks.description: Fragmentary collection of thoughts on human misery without God, epistemology, and the existential wager.

name: Johann Gottlieb Fichte
shortBio: Pioneer of German Idealism who unified Kantian critique into the absolute self-positing Ego (Ich) in the Wissenschaftslehre, establishing dialectical striving.
centralQuestion: How does the self-determining transcendental ego generate both moral autonomy and the objective material world through practical striving?

keyWorks.title: Foundations of the Science of Knowledge (Wissenschaftslehre)
keyWorks.description: Foundational text establishing the self-positing Ego and the dialectic of the Not-Self.

name: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
shortBio: German Idealist who formulated Naturphilosophie (Philosophy of Nature), arguing that nature is visible spirit and spirit invisible nature, bridging subjective and objective reality.
centralQuestion: How are nature and conscious spirit reconciled as organic polar expressions of a unified Absolute ground?

keyWorks.title: Ideas for a Philosophy of Nature
keyWorks.description: Seminal treatise developing nature as an autonomous, self-organizing dynamic organism.

keyWorks.title: System of Transcendental Idealism
keyWorks.description: Comprehensive synthesis of nature and transcendental self-consciousness culminating in aesthetic production.

name: Charles Sanders Peirce
shortBio: American logician, scientist, and founder of Pragmatism who established modern triadic semiotics, scientific fallibilism, and the pragmatic maxim.
centralQuestion: How do the conceivable practical effects of an object constitute our entire conception of that object?

keyWorks.title: How to Make Our Ideas Clear
keyWorks.description: Seminal essay defining the pragmatic maxim and the community theory of truth.

name: Gottlob Frege
shortBio: German mathematician, logician, and father of Analytic Philosophy who invented modern mathematical logic, predicate calculus, and semantic sense/reference distinction.
centralQuestion: How can the foundations of arithmetic and logical thought be objectively secured independently of subjective human psychology?

keyWorks.title: Begriffsschrift (Concept Script)
keyWorks.description: Revolutionary formal language introducing quantifiers, functions, and modern propositional logic.

keyWorks.title: On Sense and Reference (Über Sinn und Bedeutung)
keyWorks.description: Landmark paper establishing the semantic distinction between sense (mode of presentation) and reference (truth value/object).

name: Emmanuel Levinas
shortBio: French-Lithuanian philosopher who established ethics as First Philosophy, locating transcendence in the non-negotiable vulnerability and infinite demand of the Face of the Other.
centralQuestion: Why is our ethical responsibility to the Face of the Other prior to ontology, cognition, and selfhood?

keyWorks.title: Totality and Infinity
keyWorks.description: Masterwork arguing that ethics precedes ontology through the transcendent encounter with the Other.

name: Maurice Merleau-Ponty
shortBio: French phenomenologist who restored the lived body (le corps propre) and embodied sensory perception to the foundation of consciousness and reality.
centralQuestion: How does our bodily immersion in the perceptual lifeworld precede and ground all intellectual and scientific abstraction?

keyWorks.title: Phenomenology of Perception
keyWorks.description: Seminal study of bodily intentionality, sensory gestalt, and pre-reflective perceptual life.

name: Jürgen Habermas
shortBio: Leading second-generation Frankfurt School philosopher who formulated the Theory of Communicative Action, discourse ethics, and constitutional deliberative democracy.
centralQuestion: How can intersubjective communicative reason and democratic discourse secure emancipatory legitimacy against instrumental technocracy?

keyWorks.title: The Theory of Communicative Action
keyWorks.description: Two-volume work developing rational communicative lifeworld action vs. steering media systems.

keyWorks.title: Between Facts and Norms
keyWorks.description: Comprehensive philosophy of law and deliberative democracy.

name: Derek Parfit
shortBio: Oxford moral philosopher famous for Reasons and Persons (psychological reductionism of personal identity) and On What Matters (unifying Kantianism, contractualism, and consequentialism).
centralQuestion: Does personal identity consist in anything more than psychological connectedness, and what reasons do we have to care for future generations?

keyWorks.title: Reasons and Persons
keyWorks.description: Influential treatise on personal identity, future generations, and moral rationality.

keyWorks.title: On What Matters
keyWorks.description: Monumental convergence of major normative ethical systems into triple theory.

name: Anicius Manlius Severinus Boethius
shortBio: Roman statesman and philosopher regarded as the last of the Romans and first of the scholastics, whose Consolation of Philosophy and translations of Aristotle transmitted classical logic to the medieval West.
centralQuestion: How can human free will and moral responsibility coexist with divine omniscience and the eternal present?

keyWorks.title: The Consolation of Philosophy (De consolatione philosophiae)
keyWorks.description: Masterpiece on divine eternity, fortune, virtue, and providence written in prison awaiting execution.

keyWorks.title: Commentaries on Aristotle's Categories and De Interpretatione
keyWorks.description: Foundational Latin translations and commentaries forming the medieval Logica Vetus (Old Logic).
